name: Reserva
pairings: Roast meats, grilled lamb, duck à l'orange, pork, wild mushrooms, casseroles, Iberian ham, mature cheeses
notes: 100% Tempranillo, hand-harvested (Gimileo & Haro). 18 months in medium-toast American oak, bottled unfiltered. Deep ruby with tawny highlights; black fruit, liquorice, violet, vanilla, sweet spice, toasted bread. Drinking now; will evolve gracefully for 8–12 years.

name: Munfrina
pairings: Charcuterie, pasta with meat sauce, wood-fired pizza, roasted chicken, grilled pork chops
notes: 100% Dolcetto. A vibrant, fruit-forward red with bright acidity, dark cherry notes, and a classic bitter almond finish; typical drinking window used for young Dolcetto.

name: Shiraz
pairings: grilled steaks, barbecue ribs, burgers, pepperoni pizza, mature cheddar
notes: 100% Shiraz. A medium-bodied, approachable wine with ripe plum, blackberry, and subtle spice notes. The drinking window is based on typical ranges for entry-level commercial Australian Shiraz, which is designed for early consumption.

name: Bourgogne Passetoutgrains
pairings: Charcuterie, cold cuts, roasted poultry, simple pork dishes
notes: A traditional blend of Pinot Noir and Gamay. As a light Bourgogne Passetoutgrains intended for youthful consumption, this 1983 vintage is now well past its prime drinking window.

name: L'Amour Toujours
pairings: Grilled steak, roast lamb, aged cheddar, venison, hearty stews
notes: Bordeaux-style red blend from the Allée Bleue estate (founded 1690), Stellenbosch. Award-winning bottling (Double Platinum, National Wine Challenge Champion, Top 100 SA Wines). Drink window is an estimate for a premium Cape Bordeaux blend of this vintage, not a producer-published figure.

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
pairings: Grilled beef, lamb chops, hearty stews, aged cheeses
notes: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon. Produced by Viña Caliterra Ltda., Santiago. Well past typical drinking window for this tier of Chilean Cab.

name: Carte d'Or Muscadet Sèvre et Maine Sur Lie
region: Muscadet Sèvre et Maine AOC, Loire, France
pairings: Oysters, mussels, grilled fish, shrimp, goat cheese
notes: 100% Melon de Bourgogne. Sur lie ageing adds richness. Le Cleray, 12% alc. Past typical window but top Muscadet can surprise with age.

name: Don Melchor Private Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon
pairings: Prime rib, roast lamb, venison, truffled dishes, aged Gruyère
notes: Flagship icon Cabernet Sauvignon from Concha y Toro. One of Chile's most celebrated wines. Well-cellared bottles may still drink, though past optimal window.

name: Pomerol
pairings: Roast duck, filet mignon, truffled risotto, soft-ripened cheeses
notes: Merlot-dominant Pomerol. JP Moueix. 1989 is a legendary Bordeaux vintage. At or past peak but could still offer pleasure if well stored.

name: St-Émilion Grand Cru
pairings: Roast lamb, braised beef, duck confit, mature Comté
notes: Moueix proprietor. Merlot/Cabernet Franc blend. Past peak drinking window.

name: St-Émilion Grand Cru
region: St-Émilion Grand Cru Classé, Bordeaux, France
pairings: Roast beef, lamb, game birds, aged hard cheeses
notes: Vicomte P. de Lesquen, proprietor. St-Émilion Grand Cru Classé. Past typical drinking window.

name: No. 99 Baco Noir
pairings: BBQ ribs, burgers, pulled pork, pizza, cheddar
notes: 100% Baco Noir. 12.5% alc. A fruity, medium-bodied Canadian red best enjoyed young.

name: No. 99 Chardonnay
pairings: Grilled chicken, creamy pasta, lobster, brie
notes: 100% Chardonnay. 13.0% alc. Best enjoyed young.

name: NeroMàccarj
pairings: Grilled sausages, pasta alla Norma, braised lamb, pecorino
notes: 100% Nero d'Avola. Premium single-vineyard Sicilian red from a top producer. Past peak but could still surprise.

name: Cyane
pairings: Seafood, grilled fish, light salads, fresh mozzarella
notes: Siracusa DOC Bianco. Named after the nymph Cyane. From Pupillo estate in Syracuse, Sicily.

name: Cuvée Prestige Cabernet Sauvignon
pairings: Grilled steak, roast beef, lamb chops, semi-hard cheeses
notes: Grand Vin de Bordeaux. Véronique Barthe, vigneronne. Mis en bouteille au château. HVE certified.

name: Gewurztraminer Réserve
pairings: Foie gras, Munster cheese, spicy Asian cuisine, fruit tarts
notes: 100% Gewurztraminer. Réserve. Scherwiller. Aromatic Alsatian white with lychee, rose petal, and spice notes.

name: Re Federico
pairings: Grilled meats, pasta with ragù, aubergine parmigiana, aged pecorino
notes: Siracusa DOC Rosso. Likely Nero d'Avola-based. From Pupillo estate in Syracuse, Sicily.

name: Bordeaux
pairings: Grilled meats, roast chicken, charcuterie, mild cheeses
notes: Appellation Bordeaux Contrôlée. Caves de Rauzan. Bouteille à la Propriété.

name: Sancerre Les Baronnes
pairings: Goat cheese (Crottin de Chavignol), oysters, grilled white fish, asparagus
notes: 100% Sauvignon Blanc. Chavignol. Mis en bouteille au Domaine. Well past typical window.

name: Grange Bin 95
pairings: Prime rib, slow-braised short ribs, venison, aged cheddar, dark chocolate
notes: Australia's most iconic wine. Predominantly Shiraz. Dedicated to Max Schubert (1915–1994). Bottle No. AV762. Developed from observations of Bordeaux first-growth techniques, matured in new American oak hogsheads. Will age for decades.

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
pairings: Grilled ribeye, braised short ribs, roast lamb, aged Gouda
notes: Premium Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon. 14.4% alc. Should still be drinking well if properly cellared.

name: St-Émilion Grand Cru
pairings: Roast duck, filet mignon, lamb, truffled dishes, Époisses
notes: Vauthier, viticulteur à St-Émilion. 1989 is a legendary Bordeaux vintage. At or past peak.

name: Meursault
pairings: Lobster thermidor, roast chicken with cream sauce, Comté, scallops
notes: 100% Chardonnay. Domaine Faiveley, Nuits-Saint-Georges. Négociant-éleveur. Well past typical window but great Meursault can age.

name: Barolo
pairings: Braised beef, risotto with truffles, game, aged Parmigiano-Reggiano
notes: 100% Nebbiolo. La Morra. 13.5% alc. Estate bottled. Past peak but Barolo can surprise with long life.

name: Terrunyo Carmenere Block 27
region: DO Peumo, Valle del Cachapoal, Chile
pairings: Grilled lamb, beef empanadas, slow-cooked stews, smoked Gouda
notes: Entre Cordilleras, Peumo Vineyard. Premium single-vineyard Carmenere. Block 27 designates specific terroir within the estate.

name: St-Émilion Grand Cru
pairings: Roast lamb, duck confit, beef bourguignon, mature cheeses
notes: Grand Vin de Bordeaux. Mestreguilhem proprietaire, St Laurent des Combes. Mis en bouteille au château. 2016 is an excellent Bordeaux vintage.

name: Old Vine Pinotage
pairings: Braai (SA barbecue), bobotie, grilled sausages, smoked meats
notes: Old vine Pinotage from Piekenierskloof. Allée Bleue estate founded 1690. Eike Daasen.

name: Sassicaia
pairings: Bistecca alla fiorentina, roast lamb, wild boar ragù, aged Pecorino Toscano
notes: Marchesi Incisa della Rocchetta. Cabernet Sauvignon/Cabernet Franc blend. Italy's original Super Tuscan, Bolgheri's most iconic wine.

name: Barolo
pairings: Braised beef, truffle risotto, osso buco, aged Parmigiano-Reggiano
notes: 100% Nebbiolo. La Morra. Estate bottled. Should still be in a fine drinking window.

name: Sassicaia
pairings: Bistecca alla fiorentina, roast lamb, wild boar ragù, aged Pecorino Toscano
notes: Marchesi Incisa della Rocchetta. Cabernet Sauvignon/Cabernet Franc blend. Tenuta San Guido, Bolgheri. Should still be drinking beautifully.

name: St-Émilion 1er Grand Cru Classé A
pairings: Roast lamb, filet mignon, truffle dishes, foie gras, aged Comté
notes: 1er Grand Cru Classé A. Héritiers Fourcaud-Laussac. One of Bordeaux's most legendary estates. Predominantly Cabernet Franc and Merlot. At or past peak but iconic bottles can endure.

name: L'Authentique
pairings: Grilled meats, duck, cassoulet, semi-hard cheeses
notes: Francs Côtes de Bordeaux. Charming label featuring a stag in a beret and marinière. Right Bank Bordeaux blend.

name: Nubiola Barbaresco
pairings: Braised beef, risotto with porcini, roast veal, tajarin pasta, aged cheeses
notes: 100% Nebbiolo. Pelissero Giorgio, Treiso. Single-vineyard Barbaresco. Young — will benefit from cellaring.

name: Valpolicella Classico Superiore
region: Valpolicella Classico Superiore DOC, Veneto, Italy
pairings: Pizza, pasta with tomato sauce, grilled vegetables, light meats
notes: Corvina, Rondinella, Molinara blend. Historic label edition. Drink young.

name: Valpolicella Ripasso Classico Superiore
region: Valpolicella Ripasso Classico Superiore DOC, Veneto, Italy
pairings: Grilled red meats, pasta with meat ragù, hard cheeses, risotto
notes: Azienda Agricola. Ripasso method — re-fermented on Amarone grape skins for added body and complexity.

name: Sforzato dell'Orco
region: Sforzato di Valtellina DOCG, Lombardy, Italy
pairings: Braised meats, game, polenta taragna, bresaola, aged Bitto cheese
notes: 100% Nebbiolo (locally called Chiavennasca). Appassimento method — grapes partially dried before pressing. Rich, complex alpine Nebbiolo.

name: Tradizione del Nonno Riserva
region: Primitivo di Manduria DOP, Puglia, Italy
pairings: Grilled lamb, orecchiette with sausage, eggplant parmigiana, aged provolone
notes: 100% Primitivo. Riserva. Sava, Italy. Full-bodied, rich southern Italian red.

name: Patina Cabernet Franc Reserve
pairings: Roast pork, goulash, grilled meats, paprika dishes, aged cheeses
notes: 100% Cabernet Franc Reserve. Hungarian producer. Label text in Hungarian describes the wine's character.

name: Guado al Tasso
pairings: Bistecca alla fiorentina, roast lamb, wild boar, aged Pecorino, truffled dishes
notes: Tenuta Guado al Tasso. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot blend. Antinori's flagship Bolgheri Super Tuscan.

name: Persistence
pairings: Grilled ribeye steak, roasted rack of lamb, braised beef short ribs, aged cheddar cheese
notes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Syrah, Petit Verdot. A plush and full-bodied Napa blend featuring ripe blackberry, mocha, and toasted oak spice.

name: Cirò Rosso Classico Superiore
pairings: grilled lamb chops, spicy sausage, pasta bolognese, aged pecorino cheese
notes: Predominantly Gaglioppo. A rustic, medium-bodied Southern Italian red with notes of sour cherry, leather, wild herbs, and dusty tannins.

name: Côtes du Rhône Rouge
region: Côtes du Rhône, Rhône Valley, France
pairings: Grilled red meats, roasted lamb with rosemary, charcuterie, pork chops, hard cheeses
notes: Typically a blend of Grenache and Syrah. A medium-bodied, fruit-forward Southern Rhône red featuring ripe red berry fruit, mild peppery spice, and subtle garrigue notes.

name: Cuvée Alexandre Merlot
pairings: Grilled lamb chops, roasted duck breast, beef tenderloin, aged gouda
notes: Merlot blended with small amounts of Cabernet Sauvignon/Carmenere. A fully mature, classic Chilean red with complex tertiary notes of dried plum, leather, cedar, and resolved tannins.

name: El Nane
pairings: roasted red meats, pasta with wild boar ragu, grilled lamb chops, mature cheeses
notes: Typically a blend of Corvina, Corvinone, Rondinella, and Croatina. A rich, velvety Veneto red with ripe dark fruit, baking spice, and subtle dried grape notes. Vintage not visible on front label; drinking window and price estimate assume a typical current release.

name: Dry Creek Valley Reserve Zinfandel
pairings: BBQ ribs, grilled steak, wood-fired pizza, smoked brisket
notes: Mainly Zinfandel with a touch of Petite Sirah. A rich yet elegant expression of Dry Creek Valley with brambly blackberry fruit, spice, and balanced acidity.

name: Merlot - Grenache
pairings: Grilled pork chops, roasted chicken, burgers, tomato-based pasta dishes
notes: Merlot and Grenache. A simple, easy-drinking rustic Southern French red blend; based on typical IGP Pays d'Oc standards, this bottle is likely well past its prime drinking window.

name: Zweigelt Reserve
pairings: roasted duck, grilled lamb chops, beef goulash, aged cheeses
notes: 100% Zweigelt. A rich and velvety Austrian red featuring dark cherry, plum, and fine spices from oak barrique aging. Vintage not visible on front label; drinking window and pricing are estimated based on typical recent releases.

name: Prunicce
pairings: Grilled ribeye, pasta bolognese, wild boar ragu, aged pecorino cheese
notes: Typically a blend of Sangiovese and Cabernet Franc. A vibrant, medium-bodied Tuscan red with notes of dark cherries, wild herbs, and supple tannins; vintage is not visible on the front label.

name: Grand Vin du Château
pairings: Grilled lamb, roasted Mediterranean vegetables, cassoulet, pork chops, hard cheeses
notes: A blend of Carignan, Grenache, Syrah, and Mourvèdre. A rustic, medium-bodied organic red with notes of ripe dark fruit, black pepper, and wild garrigue herbs.

name: Châteauneuf-du-Pape Rouge
pairings: Roasted lamb, grilled ribeye steak, venison stew, wild boar, rosemary-infused dishes
notes: Typically a Grenache-dominated blend with Syrah and Mourvèdre. A rich, full-bodied Southern Rhône red featuring ripe dark fruit, garrigue, and black pepper notes. Vintage is not visible on the front label.

name: Neromàccarj
pairings: roasted lamb, slow-cooked beef ragù, aged pecorino cheese, wild game
notes: 100% Nero d'Avola. An intensely structured, single-vineyard Sicilian red showcasing complex notes of dark plum, leather, Mediterranean scrub, and well-integrated tertiary earthiness.

name: Cancellaia di Riparbella
pairings: Grilled ribeye steak, rosemary-roasted lamb, wild boar ragu, aged pecorino cheese
notes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc. An elegant, structured Super Tuscan with ripe dark fruits, herbal nuances, and refined tannins. Vintage is not visible on the front label; drinking window is estimated based on a typical release.

name: Saperavi Qvevri Wine
pairings: grilled lamb chops, beef stew, khachapuri, roasted game, aged cheeses
notes: 100% Saperavi. A traditional clay-vessel (Qvevri) fermented red offering deep blackberry and plum notes, firm rustic tannins, and an earthy, savory finish.

name: Langhe Nebbiolo
pairings: Truffle risotto, roasted veal, aged cheeses, wild mushroom pasta
notes: 100% Nebbiolo. A medium-bodied, classic Piedmontese red showing notes of sour cherry, dried rose petals, and tar, with the vibrant acidity and structured tannins typical of the stellar 2016 vintage.

name: Longitudine 8.10
pairings: risotto with seafood, grilled sea bass, goat cheese, vegetable tempura
notes: 100% Erbaluce; a crisp, mineral-driven white wine with high acidity and delicate citrus and floral aromatics characteristic of the Caluso/Alto Piemonte terroir.

name: Egri Bikavér
pairings: Beef goulash, roasted game, hearty stews, pork paprikash
notes: A classic Hungarian Kékfrankos-based blend. Medium-bodied and vibrant with bright dark cherry, forest floor, and warm baking spices.

name: Mirau Barolo
pairings: Bistecca alla Fiorentina, wild mushroom risotto, truffled pasta, aged Parmigiano-Reggiano, game meats
notes: 100% Nebbiolo; a traditionally styled, structured Barolo with notes of dried roses, tar, leather, and firm tannins.

name: Longitudine 26
pairings: roasted meats, aged cheeses, mushroom risotto, charcuterie
notes: 100% Nebbiolo; an elegant, expressive, and mineral-driven red typical of the cool-climate vineyards in the Lessona and Bramaterra areas.

name: Château Monconseil Gazin
pairings: roasted lamb, grilled beef, aged hard cheeses, duck confit
notes: Predominantly Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon; a medium-bodied, structured, and fruit-forward Bordeaux with typical earthy and plummy characteristics.

name: Les Vénérables
pairings: oysters, grilled fish, goat cheese, roast chicken
notes: Chardonnay; a classic, mineral-driven Chablis from old vines, showing high acidity, citrus notes, and a saline finish characteristic of the Kimmeridgian soils.

name: Réserve
pairings: roasted lamb, grilled beef, hard cheeses, charcuterie
notes: A blend dominated by Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon; a structured, fruit-forward, and approachable Bordeaux Supérieur with classic dark berry notes.

name: Marques de Casa Concha
pairings: lamb, grilled red meats, mature cheeses, spicy pasta dishes
notes: 100% Carmenere; a full-bodied, complex red with notable notes of dark fruit, spice, herbs, and soft tannins typical of the Peumo terroir.

name: Estate Reserva
pairings: goat cheese, fresh salads, shellfish, ceviche, grilled white fish
notes: 100% Sauvignon Blanc; a crisp, vibrant, and aromatic expression with classic zesty citrus and tropical fruit notes typical of the cool-climate Aconcagua region.

name: Monasterio de las Viñas Reserva
pairings: lamb chops, roast beef, aged manchego cheese, chorizo
notes: Garnacha, Tempranillo & Cariñena; a traditional, rustic, and tertiary-aged Spanish red, likely past its prime drinking window.

name: Khvanchkara
pairings: cheese plates, fruit-based desserts, walnuts, churchkhela, roasted poultry
notes: Made from Alexanderi and Mujuretuli grapes; this is a classic Georgian naturally semi-sweet red wine known for its velvety texture and prominent strawberry and raspberry notes.

name: Grande Réserve
pairings: grilled red meats, roast lamb, hard cheeses, charcuterie
notes: Primarily Merlot with Cabernet Sauvignon; a medium-bodied, classic Bordeaux blend with ripe dark fruit, integrated oak, and soft tannins.

name: Amarone della Valpolicella Classico
pairings: braised beef, game meats, aged cheeses, dark chocolate
notes: Corvina, Corvinone, and Rondinella; a full-bodied, rich, and intense red wine made from dried grapes with notes of dried fruit, spice, and tobacco.

name: Amarone della Valpolicella Classico
pairings: Braised beef, roasted game, aged cheeses, dark chocolate
notes: Corvina, Corvinone, Rondinella blend; a rich, full-bodied wine featuring intense aromas of dried fruit, cherry liqueur, and spice, with velvety tannins.

name: Brunello di Montalcino 40 Years Together
pairings: roasted game, braised beef, aged pecorino, truffle dishes
notes: 100% Sangiovese; this special edition is a structured, elegant, and long-lived expression of a classic vintage, featuring notes of cherry, tobacco, and leather.

name: Chance
pairings: Grilled steak, lamb chops, aged cheddar, wild mushroom risotto
notes: Merlot, Cabernet Franc, and Cabernet Sauvignon blend; this is a rare, age-worthy red blend from Niagara's cool-climate terroir, now well past its optimal drinking window.

name: Bolgheri Superiore
pairings: Bistecca alla Fiorentina, roasted rack of lamb, braised short ribs, aged hard cheeses
notes: A blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, and Petit Verdot; a prestigious, powerful, and structured 'Super Tuscan' with remarkable aging potential.

name: Reserva Tinto
pairings: roasted lamb, grilled steaks, mature cheeses, game meats
notes: A field blend of traditional Douro grapes; elegant and structured with concentrated dark fruit, spice, and polished tannins typical of a premium Reserva from the region.

name: Ogga
pairings: roasted lamb, grilled ribeye steak, mature manchego cheese, game meats
notes: 100% Tempranillo; an ultra-premium, selection-based cuvée from old vines, offering a powerful, sophisticated, and age-worthy expression of Rioja with refined tannins.

name: Château Bel-Air
pairings: roasted lamb, beef tenderloin, mushroom risotto, hard aged cheeses
notes: Predominantly Merlot with Cabernet Franc; a classic, elegant, and velvety Pomerol showing ripe plum, black cherry, and subtle earthy spice.

name: Do Ut Des
pairings: Bistecca alla Fiorentina, roasted lamb, wild boar ragu, aged pecorino cheese
notes: Blend of Sangiovese, Merlot, and Cabernet Sauvignon; a powerful, structured Super Tuscan with ripe dark fruit, integrated oak, and velvety tannins.

name: Montaperto
pairings: roasted meats, grilled steak, pasta with tomato sauce, aged cheeses
notes: 100% Sangiovese; a classic, structured Chianti Classico with elegant notes of red cherry, earth, and supple tannins.

name: Sainte-Radegonde
pairings: Grilled steak, lamb chops, roast beef, hard cheeses
notes: A blend of Merlot and Cabernet Franc; this is a structured yet accessible Right Bank Bordeaux with notes of ripe dark fruit, graphite, and silky tannins.

name: Les Sources
pairings: Roasted lamb, grilled steak, hard cheeses, mushroom risotto
notes: Merlot and Cabernet Franc blend; a medium-bodied, approachable Bordeaux Supérieur with ripe red fruit and earthy undertones.

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
pairings: grilled steak, braised short ribs, aged cheddar, roasted lamb
notes: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon; a bold, full-bodied California red with notes of dark berries, oak, and smooth tannins, typical of accessible Napa/North Coast style blends.

name: Octopoda
pairings: grilled octopus, lamb chops, steak frites, aged cheddar
notes: Primarily Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah blend; a bold, fruit-forward California red with notes of dark berries, cocoa, and supple tannins.

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
pairings: grilled ribeye steak, braised short ribs, aged cheddar, roasted lamb
notes: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon; a bold, fruit-forward Napa Valley red with layers of black currant, cocoa, and toasted oak.

name: Gran Terroir de Los Andes Los Lingues
pairings: roasted lamb, grilled beef, spicy dishes, mature cheeses
notes: 100% Carmenere; a concentrated, structured wine with hallmark notes of black fruit, spice, and subtle bell pepper typical of the Los Lingues terroir.
